ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure there is a diagonal line from point A in the upper left through point B in the middle to point C in the lower right. The given condition states that ABC is a dusk line; from A to D is the upper horizontal line segment, and from B to E is the middle horizontal line segment, so AD and BE represent parts of parallels; from D to B and from E to C are vertical line segments, so BD and CE represent parts of meridians. It can be seen from the figure that D is at the same latitude as A and the same meridian as B, while E is at the same latitude as B and the same meridian as C; in longitude position, A is on the west side, B/D are in the middle, and C/E are on the east side. Then reason: the ratio of the time difference between A and B to the time difference between B and C is 1:2. Treating the whole dusk line ABC as spanning a 12-hour longitude difference, AB corresponds to 4 hours, and BC corresponds to 8 hours. A and B are both on the dusk line, indicating local sunset; B is 4 hours of longitude difference east of A, so the local sunset time at the latitude of point B is 4 hours later than that at the latitude of point A. Sunrise and sunset local times are symmetric about noon at 12 o'clock, so the local sunrise time at the latitude of point B is 4 hours earlier than that at the latitude of point A. E is at the same latitude as B, and D is at the same latitude as A, so the local sunrise time at point E is 4 hours earlier than that at point D. Also because the meridian where E is located is 8 hours east of the meridian where D is located, when converting the same local-time event into a unified moment, the eastern location will occur another 8 hours earlier. Therefore the sunrise at point E is earlier than that at point D by a total of 4 hours + 8 hours = 12 hours.

Read the figure and answer: <image1> If the ratio of the time difference between A and B to the time difference between B and C is 1:2, is the sunrise time at point E earlier or later than that at point D, and by how many hours?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
First describe the image: in the figure there is a diagonal line from point A in the upper left through point B in the middle to point C in the lower right. The given condition states that ABC is a dusk line; from A to D is the upper horizontal line segment, and from B to E is the middle horizontal line segment, so AD and BE represent parts of parallels; from D to B and from E to C are vertical line segments, so BD and CE represent parts of meridians. It can be seen from the figure that D is at the same latitude as A and the same meridian as B, while E is at the same latitude as B and the same meridian as C; in longitude position, A is on the west side, B/D are in the middle, and C/E are on the east side.

Then reason: the ratio of the time difference between A and B to the time difference between B and C is 1:2. Treating the whole dusk line ABC as spanning a 12-hour longitude difference, AB corresponds to 4 hours, and BC corresponds to 8 hours. A and B are both on the dusk line, indicating local sunset; B is 4 hours of longitude difference east of A, so the local sunset time at the latitude of point B is 4 hours later than that at the latitude of point A. Sunrise and sunset local times are symmetric about noon at 12 o'clock, so the local sunrise time at the latitude of point B is 4 hours earlier than that at the latitude of point A. E is at the same latitude as B, and D is at the same latitude as A, so the local sunrise time at point E is 4 hours earlier than that at point D. Also because the meridian where E is located is 8 hours east of the meridian where D is located, when converting the same local-time event into a unified moment, the eastern location will occur another 8 hours earlier. Therefore the sunrise at point E is earlier than that at point D by a total of 4 hours + 8 hours = 12 hours.
